statusNote: Compared with Run 1: the blue slope was picked up and pressed onto the plate first, and the pink brick was added afterwards (reference order is pink first, then blue). Cycle 5.3 s vs 5.5 s.

elements.label: Idle before cycle
elements.observed: Three loose parts on the table; one hand resting still at the bottom right edge, another at the top edge.

elements.label: Reach and grasp blue 2×2 slope
elements.observed: Lower right hand moves to the blue slope and picks it up with finger and thumb. The upper hand enters and hovers near the pink brick without touching it.
elements.flag: Blue picked first; Run 1 picks pink first.

elements.label: Carry blue slope
elements.observed: Blue slope carried in the lower hand toward the plate, which stays on the table.
elements.flag: Blue goes to the bare plate; Run 1 carries blue to a plate with pink on it.

elements.label: Hold the base plate
elements.observed: Upper hand moves to the plate and its fingertips rest on the plate's top edge while the lower hand works. The plate stays on the table.
elements.flag: Plate held during the blue step, not the pink step.

elements.label: Position and orient blue slope
elements.observed: Blue slope set against the plate by the lower hand fingers; hands hide the exact stud position.
elements.flag: Boundary with pressing hidden by hands.

elements.label: Press blue slope down
elements.observed: Lower hand fingers stay on the blue slope and press it on the plate; hands hide most of it. Blue visibly seated on the plate by 4.0 s.
elements.flag: Blue pressed before pink; Run 1 presses pink first.

elements.label: Reach and grasp pink 1×6 brick
elements.observed: Upper hand lets go of the plate, moves back to the pink brick still on the table and closes on it at about 4.2-4.4 s.
elements.flag: Pink picked second; Run 1 picks it first.

elements.label: Place pink brick on plate
elements.observed: Pink brick lifted and moved to the plate (blurred at 4.6 s), lowered lengthwise next to the blue slope; the lower hand grips the plate's near edge.
elements.flag: Pink placed after blue, beside it.

elements.label: Hold the base plate
elements.observed: Lower hand fingers grip the near edge of the plate while the upper hand works on the brick.
elements.flag: Second plate hold, by the other hand.

elements.label: Press pink brick down
elements.observed: Upper hand fingers press along the pink brick; hands hide most of the assembly. Pink visible on the plate beside blue by 5.0 s.
elements.flag: Hands hide the pressing and exact studs.

elements.label: Release and set down
elements.observed: Both hands let go and withdraw to the frame edges by 6.6 s. The assembly was not turned or lifted visibly.
elements.flag: No visible turning of the assembly, unlike Run 1.

elements.label: Idle after cycle
elements.observed: Finished assembly alone on the table, tilted slightly; one hand resting at the bottom right edge and one at the top edge.

processData: Which hand holds the plate and when
Hold and press durations per part
Idle time before and after the cycle
limitations: Hands hide the pressing and exact stud rows for both parts
Boundary between positioning and pressing the blue slope is not visible
Parts are small in the frame so stud counts are approximate

source.note: Claude Code, frame by frame at 0.1 s steps

differences: Blue slope picked by the lower hand at 1.3-1.8 s and seated on the plate by about 4.0 s; Run 1 places pink first and blue second.
Pink brick stays on the table untouched until 3.9 s, then is lifted by the upper hand (4.2-4.6 s) and placed at about 4.8 s.
Plate is held by the upper hand (about 1.9-3.9 s) during the blue step, then by the lower hand (about 4.6-6.2 s) during the pink step; Run 1 holds once, during pink.
Plate shifts on the table at about 3.9-4.0 s as the upper hand lets go; the assembly is not turned between steps as in Run 1.

finalState.note: Pink 1×6 brick on the plate's second stud column, full length; blue 2×2 slope over columns 3-4 beside it, facing outward; one white column free. Assembly sits slightly tilted. Exact blue rows are approximate.
